changes: Copy the tracking key, endpoint and environment together for server setup.
Use the configured tracking endpoint and validate the environment in setup examples.
upgrade: Use the verified CLI and tracking release, then restart running CLI and MCP processes.
Keep existing keys and permissions; save the endpoint and environment alongside the key in server configuration.
Preserve event IDs, delivery receipts, capture settings and working application changes.
release.recovery: Restore the previous dependency and app commit after checking service support. Keep pending delivery IDs. Sent messages, deleted history and newly collected data cannot be undone by reinstalling a package.

support.exceptions: Keep a working older installation temporarily with a reason, owner, next action and review date. Recheck within 30 days; a review date never stops capture automatically.
support.enforcement: Advisory. No version-based rejection of existing tracking or automatic customer messaging changes.
support.scope: Newer releases receive fixes. Older installations receive upgrade help; no indefinite promise to backport fixes. Retirement requires a published notice and at least 180 days, except a separately reviewed urgent security response.

limitations: Release requirements do not prove source access, deployment, history coverage, recording consent, worker health or contact permission.
